newsitem.title: INDIA: India urges kites and lights to mark freedom.
newsitem.headline: India urges kites and lights to mark freedom.

text.p: India has appealed to its citizens to fly kites, hoist flags and hold marches at the crack of dawn on Friday to celebrate the 50th anniversary of independence from Britain.

"Let there be balloons, kites, posters, pamphlets, flags and indeed all forms of public celebrations so that the festivities and the atmosphere convey our innermost feelings not only to the country but to the entire world," Human Resource Development Minister S.R. Bommai said on Wednesday.
India won independence at the stroke of midnight on August 14-15, 1947, after a decades-long struggle against British colonial rule.
The government has decided to mark the anniversary with year-long celebrations that will begin on Thursday evening, August 14.
"Every rickshaw, every car, every house should be illuminated," Bommai told a news conference in the capital.
"All government buildings, world heritage, national heritage and freedom sites will be illuminated on the nights of the 14th and 15th," the government said in a statement.
Bommai asked citizens to form long human chains by holding hands on Friday, and visit sites sacred to India's freedom struggle.
"We are the largest democracy of the world and the 50 years of independence are full of success stories," Bommai said.
Bommai said the government had decided to relax a rule that that requires citizens to obtain permission before being allowed to fly the national flag.
The minister urged "all farmers, soldiers, labourers, workers, scientists, engineers, doctors, artists, traders, industrialists and indeed all sections of society" to take part.
A special logo bearing the colours of India's flag -- saffron, white and light green -- and the numeral 50 can be used on banners, caps, T-shirts, balloons, stickers and flags, he said.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral will receive thousands of marchers one hour before midnight on Thursday at Vijay Chowk (Victory Square) near Delhi's British-built presidential palace in a "March of the Nation," officials said.
Laser shows and fireworks will mark the celebration.
At midnight, parliament will to hold a special session to listen to recorded speeches of independence leaders Mahatma Gandhi and Jawharlal Nehru, the nation's first prime minister.

Also at midnight, performing artists from India and neighbouring Pakistan will hold cultural shows at the Wagah border point in Punjab symbolising reconciliation after the massacre of hundreds of thousands during the partition of the subcontinent in 1947.
On Friday morning, Gujral will deliver the customary Independence Day address from the ramparts of the 17th century Red Fort in the old quarter of Delhi.
